Per-residue uptake as a length-weighted mean across covering peptides

Source: R/residue_level_average.R
residue_level_average.Rd

A fast, simple companion to residue_deconvolution(): for each residue, at each Protein.State/replicate/timepoint, computes a weighted mean of percent deuteration across every peptide that covers that residue, with each peptide weighted by 1 / nb_exch_deut(peptide) - i.e. shorter, more localized peptides contribute more than long ones. No kinetic model and no smoothing between residues are used.

Usage

residue_level_average(df, protein_length)

Arguments

df

data.frame, output of output_tp() called with percent = TRUE. Percent deuteration is required here (not uptake in Daltons): it is already normalized per peptide length, so a weighted average across peptides of different lengths is meaningful. Raw uptake is an extensive quantity (scales with peptide length) and averaging it directly across peptides of different lengths would not be - use residue_deconvolution() for uptake-based, length-aware reconstruction.

protein_length

integer, total number of residues in the protein.

Value

data.frame with one row per residue and Deut.Time, and one column per Protein.State/replicate, giving the weighted mean percent deuteration across all peptides covering that residue. NA where no peptide covers a residue.

Details

Unlike residue_deconvolution(), this does not separate the contribution of overlapping peptides, so a residue near the edge of a long peptide still carries some signal from its neighbors. Use it as a quick baseline to compare with residue_deconvolution().

See also

residue_deconvolution(), output_tp(), nb_exch_deut()

Examples

file_nm <- system.file("extdata", "All_results_table.csv", package = "HDXBoxeR")
a <- output_tp(file_nm, percent = TRUE)
#> Protein.States used: Unbound bound
#> Deut.times used: 3.00s 60.00s 1800.00s 72000.00s
#> 29 peptide row(s) dropped: 29 not measured in every state, 0 with fewer than 2 replicate value(s)
#> Number of replicates used: Unbound=3 bound=3
#> no csv file written
res <- residue_level_average(a, protein_length = 225)
